objective.statement: Classify every regular time signature as simple or compound and duple, triple or quadruple.
successCriteria: I know the simple and compound time signatures and their beat notes.
I can count the beats by dividing the top number by 3 in compound time.
I can tell which regular time signature a rhythm is in.

explanation.text: A regular time signature is one with two, three or four beats in the bar: duple, triple or quadruple time. Each can be simple (the beat divides into two) or compound (the beat divides into three). That gives six families, and all of them are common enough to be asked at Grade 4, though a few are rare in real music. Simple time: the bottom number names the beat note, and the top number counts the beats. So 2/8, 3/8 and 4/8 have two, three and four quaver beats; 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 have crotchet beats; 2/2, 3/2 and 4/2 have minim beats.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 2/8, each with two quaver beats.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: quaver, quaver. Bar 2: quaver, quaver.

explanation.text: Compound time: the beat is a dotted note, so the top number counts the notes that make up the beats, three to a beat. Divide it by three. 6/4, 9/4 and 12/4 have two, three and four dotted-minim beats; 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 have dotted-crotchet beats; 6/16, 9/16 and 12/16 have dotted-quaver beats.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 6/4, each with two dotted minims.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted minim, dotted minim. Bar 2: dotted minim, dotted minim.

explanation.caption: 6/4: six crotchets, two dotted-minim beats. Compound duple.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 12/16 with four dotted quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted quaver, dotted quaver, dotted quaver, dotted quaver.

explanation.caption: 12/16: twelve semiquavers, four dotted-quaver beats. Compound quadruple.

explanation.text: Simple: top number = beats. Compound: top number ÷ 3 = beats. The bottom number names the note counted, and in compound time three of them make a beat.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 9/4 with three dotted minims.

steps: Nine crotchets in the bar: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 beats.
Each beat is three crotchets, a dotted minim.
Three dotted-minim beats: compound triple time.
demonstration.textAlternative: A bar of 9/4 with three dotted minims: compound triple time.

recap: Regular times are duple, triple or quadruple, simple or compound.
Simple: the top number counts the beats. Compound: divide it by 3.
Compound beats are dotted notes: dotted minim over 4, dotted crotchet over 8, dotted quaver over 16.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 4 outcome 1 and First Steps Grade 4 section 3 (pp. 80-81). OPEN_QUESTIONS Q7: the commonly used regular signatures are asked, including 2/8 and 12/4 (the book calls them rare but examinable); x/16 simple times are excluded. 4/8 is taught and asked in words, but it is never used in 'add the time signature to this rhythm' questions because the same rhythm also fits 2/4 (the book's own point: the difference is only whether the beat is a crotchet or a quaver). A rhythm is only asked when exactly one regular signature fits it (tested).
